name: דָּן
summary: Jacob’s fifth son, the first born to him by Bilhah, Rachel’s maid, and the tribe named after him, whose camp set out last of all from Sinai as the rearguard of the camps (Num 10:25). Rachel named him from the verb: דָּנַנִּי אֱלֹהִים, “God has judged me”, taken up her cause and given her a son (Gen 30:6). The name is the verb’s own form, “he judged” or “judging, judge”, and Jacob’s blessing plays on it, “Dan shall judge (יָדִין) his people as one of the tribes of Israel” (Gen 49:16); Samson, of the clan of the Danites, judged Israel twenty years (Jdg 13:2; 15:20).

evidence.note: וַתֹּאמֶר רָחֵל דָּנַנִּי אֱלֹהִים … עַל כֵּן קָרְאָה שְׁמוֹ דָּן: the name given from the verb.
דָּן יָדִין עַמּוֹ, “Dan shall judge his people”: the blessing on the name.
“The standard of the camp of the sons of Dan set out, the rearguard (מְאַסֵּף) of all the camps, and over its host Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.”
The camp of Dan on the north side, under Ahiezer; it set out last (2:31).
The sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s maid: Dan and Naphtali.
Moses’ blessing: “Dan is a lion’s whelp; he leaps from Bashan.”
Manoah, Samson’s father, “of the family of the Danites (הַדָּנִי)”.
Samson “judged (וַיִּשְׁפֹּט) Israel in the days of the Philistines twenty years”.
The city Laish renamed Dan “after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel”.

note: TIPNR has the man Dan@Gen.30.6 and a place record for the city and territory of Dan; only the man is tagged. The bdb key d.bh.ad also holds the city (Gen 14:14, Jdg 18:29, “from Dan to Beersheba”) and Ezk 27:19 וְדָן, which may be a place Vedan; about 25 more of the name’s tokens are filed under the verb’s key d.bh.aa by spelling. The name has the form of the qal perfect דָּן, “he judged”, as in Gen 15:14 and Jer 22:16, or of the participle, “one who judges”.
